subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported public-exposure recipe with separate admin and mobile pairing hostnames so browser SSO can protect Control UI while mobile wss setup-code bootstrap stays OpenClaw-authenticated?
rationale: Current main covers the reported iOS runtime failures, but recommending a public mobile pairing hostname changes the documented security posture and needs maintainer approval before a docs or product fix is queued.

options.title: Document split-hostname recipe
options.body: Add security-reviewed docs for an SSO-protected admin hostname plus a mobile-safe wss hostname, including trustedProxies, allowedOrigins, token/device-auth boundaries, and validation steps.

options.title: Keep public pairing undocumented
options.body: Treat public mobile bootstrap endpoints as unsupported for now and steer users toward Tailnet, Tailscale Serve, or SSH tunnel paths.

options.title: Track as broader one-step pairing
options.body: Fold only the onboarding friction into the existing one-step mobile setup work and leave public exposure topology out of that issue.

recommendation.title: Document split-hostname recipe
recommendation.body: Add security-reviewed docs for an SSO-protected admin hostname plus a mobile-safe wss hostname, including trustedProxies, allowedOrigins, token/device-auth boundaries, and validation steps.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history match for the route fallback, current docs, and security/product boundary touched by the remaining ask.
